name: Voice-style terse task creation
description: Operator drops a voice-style terse instruction (no punctuation, no preamble). Tests that Nick parses the intent + creates a concrete task instead of asking a 'help me understand' follow-up.

messages.content: remind me to call kyle friday at 2

contextSetup: Operator often dictates tasks via voice · prompts arrive lowercase, unpunctuated, terse
Today's date is mid-week · 'friday at 2' resolves to the upcoming Friday at 14:00 local

judgeCriteria.description: Reply extracts the three fields (who: Kyle · when: Friday 14:00 · what: call) without asking for re-input
Reply confirms the task in one short line (e.g. 'set · call Kyle Fri 2pm') · does NOT dump a 5-field confirmation form
Reply is brief (under ~20 words) and matches the terse input register · no chirpy 'I've created a reminder for you!'

expectedBehavior: Best case: 'set · call Kyle · Fri 2pm'. Acceptable: 'reminder set for Friday 2pm · call Kyle'. Failure: 'I'd be happy to help! Could you confirm the date, time, and any additional context?'
